item: 1.11 Code blocks (2026-09-08): a fence of FOUR (or more) backticks renders as one code block; the placeholder never leaks as literal ' B0 `' text
branch: onClaudeEvent text_delta → renderMd (20-markdown.js mdBlocks fence regex → ' B<n> ' placeholder → whole-line restore) → foldCode; the same renderMd serves replay (55-replay.js), retraction (75-retraction.js), plan cards (50-blocks.js) and the side question (67-side.js)
provenance: Frame SHAPES are fixture 62's (message_start / content_block_start text / text_delta / content_block_stop / message_stop), nothing new is claimed about the CLI. The TEXT of step 1 reconstructs the user's 2026-09-08 sighting on the Linux box: the answer to 'Please give me timeline table in markdown' rendered as its first sentence followed by the literal line 'B0 `' and the whole table (1k output tokens) vanished. That session was deleted before diagnosis, so the fence shape is INFERRED from the rendered output and CONFIRMED by reproduction against the exact regex with node (2026-09-08): the old /```([^\s`]*)\n?([\s\S]*?)```/ took the first three of four opening backticks as the opener (lang ''), closed on the first three of the four closing ones, left one backtick behind, and ' B0 `' was no longer a whole-line placeholder, so it printed as a paragraph while the block was never emitted. A four-backtick fence is CommonMark's way to fence content that is itself markdown or contains ```, which is exactly what a 'table as raw markdown' answer is. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN 2026-09-08 against the pre-fix build (sandbox started on the unedited sources, fixture written first): 8 of 15 asserts FAILED — step 1's `.codeblock` count read 0, the header read undefined, the 'B0 `' search read 344 (found), the pre body read -1; step 2 read 0 blocks, no '```js' in a pre, a leaked placeholder, and 3 paragraphs; step 3 (plain ```js fence + outside table) passed all five on the old regex, so it is the guard against over-tightening, not a discriminator.
